# What the gate (scripts/check_frozen_files.sh) enforces:
#
#  * A row names the EXACT NEW BLOB, never just the path: a path-scoped waiver
#    would excuse every future edit to the file. Edit it again and the row stops
#    applying.
#  * A row that is no longer needed (its blob equals the pin) fails the gate and
#    must be deleted.
#  * A row for a path that is not in the manifest fails.
#  * A live row states its delta FROM THE PIN in exactly one clause,
#    `PIN-DELTA: +A/-D`, where A/D are what
#    `git diff --numstat --diff-algorithm=myers <pin-blob> <waived-blob>` prints.
#    Moving the pin ratifies every line between the pin and the waived blob, so
#    a row that counts only the increment since an earlier waiver is red. The
#    number says how big the move is; whether the prose accounts for all of it
#    is still read, not computed.

# movement already on main until it is ratified (the pin moves to the blob and
# the row is deleted; see scripts/frozen-files.txt) or reverted.

SpecCx::block first offers each instruction to verify_output_trust_ir::LocalSlots::step (not frozen; shared with eval_ir_block, which also evaluates inlined callees), handing it the module, the function and the block being evaluated. Every Alloca goes there: it is admitted as a slot only when admit_local_slot finds its type a modeled scalar (not a pointer, not 128 bits), no count and no align, and every use of its address in the whole function, by trust-ir's exhaustive Inst::uses_value walk (terminators included), the address of a non-volatile Load or Store of exactly its type with no explicit align (so naturally aligned, as trust-ir's interpreter reads align: None) in its own block, and never a Store's value; otherwise it is refused, naming the first foreign block by id or the misuse, as the catch-all eval_ir_inst refused every Alloca before. A Load or Store whose address is an admitted slot reads or writes the slot's latest stored value: a load before any store is refused, and a store is refused unless its value's declared SSA type is the slot's type (trust-ir's eval_store expect_ty). WHAT PART B NEWLY ACCEPTS, where the pin refused the whole object: (1) A RELOCATION IN A DATA SECTION, when every relocation of that section is this one shape: the section is initialized data (not zero-fill); the relocation is an absolute 64-bit pointer (Mach-O raw type 0 ARM64_RELOC_UNSIGNED with length 3; ELF raw type 257 R_AARCH64_ABS64) and not pc-relative; its offset lies on a pointer slot of the M_cg global whose symbol covers it, a slot being an offset where that global's initializer has a `Constant::SymbolAddr`; it is the only relocation on that slot; its target is a symbol (not a section), LOCAL, that is this object's own data-symbol definition, in initialized data, of the M_cg global the initializer names; that target global is immutable, not thread-local, and shares its name with no other M_cg global or function; the addend is the initializer's where the format keeps it (Mach-O: in place, compared by the image comparison, with a zero record addend; ELF: `r_addend`, over in-place zero bytes); AND ALL OF: (a) 0 <= addend < the length of the target's M_cg image (one past the end refuses, and so does every pointer to an empty image); (b) the record's own symbol, the one covering the relocation, is LOCAL; (c) the record's section and the target's are each ordinary data by the section header (`ordinary_data`): on Mach-O the whole flags word is 0 (type S_REGULAR, no attribute bit) and the section is `__TEXT,__const`, `__DATA,__const` or `__DATA,__data`; on ELF the section is SHT_PROGBITS with sh_flags exactly SHF_ALLOC or exactly SHF_ALLOC|SHF_WRITE; every other type, attribute, flag bit or name refuses; (d) the target's section is the read-only one (Mach-O `__TEXT,__const`; ELF sh_flags exactly SHF_ALLOC); (e) no symbol defined in the record's section or in the target's is weak (`defines_a_weak_symbol`); (f) the file header's flags word holds no bit but MH_SUBSECTIONS_VIA_SYMBOLS on Mach-O (set or clear) and is 0 on ELF (`plain_header_flags`); (dd) the record's symbol and the target's each carry exactly the binding and visibility `expected_symbol` gives their M_cg global's linkage and visibility, so with (b) and the LOCAL target both M_cg globals are internal or private. A section that fails any of these is refused with the pin's kind and text (DataImage, `data section .. carries relocations: pointer-bearing statics are refused`). (2) THE INITIALIZER IMAGE OF A POINTER RECORD (`pointer_record_image`): an immutable, non-thread-local, uniquely named M_cg global of `repr(packed(1))` struct type whose fields are contiguous from offset 0 and fill its size, each a `ptr` initialized by a `SymbolAddr` or a `[u8; n]` initialized by exactly n raw bytes, at least one `ptr`. It is tried only where `initializer_image` returns None, so every image the pin computed is computed by the same code; the pin imaged no aggregate: it refused a data section holding such a record's relocation as one that carries relocations (read from the pin's bind, where that check comes before the image check), and an unrelocated such global in initialized data as one it cannot image. Conditions (a), (b), (e) and (dd) are exercised on hand-built parsed objects only. Parser refusals are exercised through `CompiledObject::parse`, on a Mach-O file pointer_record_tests.rs writes field by field or on objects trust-cg emits, patched: most in one field, some by adding a symbol, a symbol table or a section header and moving or renumbering what refers to it. (iv) Fields the reader does not use, on which part B was not found to depend (examples, not a complete list: the Mach-O header's reserved word and the LC_SEGMENT_64 command fields, ELF st_other bits 2-7, e_version, e_entry and e_ph* are unread too, and e_shentsize need only be at least 64): on Mach-O, every n_desc bit but N_WEAK_DEF, N_WEAK_REF and N_SYMBOL_RESOLVER (N_ALT_ENTRY and N_NO_DEAD_STRIP among them; (e) is what the admission relies on instead of N_ALT_ENTRY), a section's reserved words, the align of every section but `__TEXT,__text`, the contents of LC_DYSYMTAB, the contents of LC_BUILD_VERSION, LC_VERSION_MIN_MACOSX and LC_LINKER_OPTION (each may repeat), the number of LC_SEGMENT_64 commands (their sections are numbered in command order), and the header's sizeofcmds; in a code section one ARM64_RELOC_ADDEND entry is accepted before a relocation of any type at its address. On ELF: e_ident beyond the magic, class and byte order; a data symbol's st_size (data extents come from symbol order); a data section's sh_entsize, sh_link, sh_info and sh_addralign (the flag bits that give the first three a meaning are refused by (c)); a relocation section's sh_addr, sh_offset alignment and sh_addralign. Neither format compares a zero-fill global's bytes, and globals are keyed by name. A data global M_cg declares external with default visibility is listed in `verified_globals` in an ELF PIC object, as on the pin, although a shared-object link leaves its symbol preemptible (bodies get `non_preemptible` false there, data globals no such mark); nothing outside the tests read `verified_globals` until 2026-11-15 (the Rust-only S2a DeadTails consumer is now removed; verified_globals gives no tail grade authority), and the admission's record and target are LOCAL by (b), (dd) and the target rule. The writability of the RECORD's section is not constrained (under PIC the loader fills the pointer). On Mach-O three section names are admitted for data, and that no linker treats one of them specially is tested only for the two that hold a location record and its file name (`__DATA,__const` and `__TEXT,__const`; trust-cg writes `__DATA,__data` too), with the one linker of (ii). (v) The carried documentation correction is comment-only, a git diff fact no test executes. (vi) `ordinary_zero_fill`'s header restriction is tested only on hand-built CompiledObject values (compiled_object_reader a_zero_fill_global_is_listed_only_under_an_ordinary_header_with_a_fitting_zero_image: Mach-O `__DATA,__bss` with an attribute bit, Mach-O `__DATA,__common` and ELF `.bss` with SHF_ALLOC only each leave the global unlisted); no test exercises it refusing on an object trust-cg emitted (no test makes an emitted zero-fill header non-ordinary: f1_compile turn_into_zero_fill patches an emitted header into an ordinary one), and that a linker may place a zero-fill section of another name or flags differently is a reading of the formats. ORACLE-FREEZE-MOVES-20261110 INDEXED-FIELD COMPOUND ROUTE (2026-11-10, eb5684db55; DQ THIR-INDEXED-FIELD-COMPOUND-1; a second reader, not its author, re-read the increment against the exact old blob fe0cf10c8d, and a fresh refuter checked this row): a bounded direct-THIR lowering capability expansion. It is NOT BYTE-IDENTICAL and NOT a REFUSES-MORE claim; it is the same class as the ordered shared-slice and Unit-literal accounts below, and it ADMITS NEW lowered bodies. The increment fe0cf10c8d -> f73a1fad76 is +6/-0: one `// Trust:` comment and one early route in LowerCx::lower_assign_op. The route sits after lower_temporary_projection_assign and before the raw-entry field route. It calls indexed_field_assignment.rs::lower_indexed_local_field_assign_op and returns None when that call owns the place. Before, `a[i].f op= rhs` on an SSA local array of a registered flat struct of integer, bool, char, f32 or f64 fields fell through to the `AssignOp(non-local place)` refusal. Now it lowers, in this order: RHS once, then the index once; a re-read of the live array, refused if the array acquired storage or changed type; the bounds assert with its obligation row (a literal out-of-range index then seals Unreachable); ExtractElement and ExtractField; the shared checked emit_arith_binop, with the same overflow, divide-by-zero, MIN/-1 and shift asserts as `x = x op e` (a refusal or divergence owns the route); InsertField, InsertElement and an SSA rebind. After a plan hit, every refusal or divergence (RHS, index, storage change, literal bounds or arithmetic) returns true, so no fallback route re-evaluates an operand. A plan miss returns false and the old routes run unchanged. The plan needs an Index whose base is a VarRef local (index_place_local), so it cannot take a deref place from the raw-entry or `*r` routes. The delegated planner and emitter were unfrozen producer code before this commit, as the plain-assignment route they share was at the b9c pin; this commit pins indexed_field_assignment.rs BYTE-IDENTICAL at 4ff1c20f3a8cb0b0b3a109397d81b2b2b910d4f3, following the ordered_slice_match.rs precedent, so a later edit to what this route lowers needs its own row. To the oracle this SAMPLES MORE: the new bodies reach the unchanged crate-seam differential. No encoder, differential, splice tripwire, admission, proven-output gate or proof-authority token in this file moves, and the direct lane stays ObligationBearingPending with no proof authority. On the opt-in -Ztrust-cg-frontend=trust-ir lane, such bodies may now reach emitted code under the unchanged admission and proven-output gates; that is the new admission this row discloses. ORACLE-FREEZE-MOVES-20261110 INDEXED-FIELD COMPOUND ROUTE (2026-11-10, eb5684db55; DQ THIR-INDEXED-FIELD-COMPOUND-1; a second reader, not its author, re-read the increment against the exact old blob fe0cf10c8d, and a fresh refuter checked this row): a bounded direct-THIR lowering capability expansion. The increment fe0cf10c8d -> f73a1fad76 is +6/-0: one `// Trust:` comment and one early route in LowerCx::lower_assign_op. The route sits after lower_temporary_projection_assign and before the raw-entry field route. It calls indexed_field_assignment.rs::lower_indexed_local_field_assign_op and returns None when that call owns the place. Before, `a[i].f op= rhs` on an SSA local array of a registered flat struct of integer, bool, char, f32 or f64 fields fell through to the `AssignOp(non-local place)` refusal. Now it lowers, in this order: RHS once, then the index once; a re-read of the live array, refused if the array acquired storage or changed type; the bounds assert with its obligation row (a literal out-of-range index then seals Unreachable); ExtractElement and ExtractField; the shared checked emit_arith_binop, with the same overflow, divide-by-zero, MIN/-1 and shift asserts as `x = x op e` (a refusal or divergence owns the route); InsertField, InsertElement and an SSA rebind. After a plan hit, every refusal or divergence (RHS, index, storage change, literal bounds or arithmetic) returns true, so no fallback route re-evaluates an operand. A plan miss returns false and the old routes run unchanged. The plan needs an Index whose base is a VarRef local (index_place_local), so it cannot take a deref place from the raw-entry or `*r` routes. The delegated planner and emitter were unfrozen producer code before this commit, as the plain-assignment route they share was at the b9c pin; this commit pins indexed_field_assignment.rs BYTE-IDENTICAL at 4ff1c20f3a8cb0b0b3a109397d81b2b2b910d4f3, following the ordered_slice_match.rs precedent, so a later edit to what this route lowers needs its own row. The route sits after lower_temporary_projection_assign and before the raw-entry field route. It calls indexed_field_assignment.rs::lower_indexed_local_field_assign_op and returns None when that call owns the place. Before, `a[i].f op= rhs` on an SSA local array of a registered flat struct of integer, bool, char, f32 or f64 fields fell through to the `AssignOp(non-local place)` refusal. Now it lowers, in this order: RHS once, then the index once; a re-read of the live array, refused if the array acquired storage or changed type; the bounds assert with its obligation row (a literal out-of-range index then seals Unreachable); ExtractElement and ExtractField; the shared checked emit_arith_binop, with the same overflow, divide-by-zero, MIN/-1 and shift asserts as `x = x op e` (a refusal or divergence owns the route); InsertField, InsertElement and an SSA rebind. After a plan hit, every refusal or divergence (RHS, index, storage change, literal bounds or arithmetic) returns true, so no fallback route re-evaluates an operand. A plan miss returns false and the old routes run unchanged. The plan needs an Index whose base is a VarRef local (index_place_local), so it cannot take a deref place from the raw-entry or `*r` routes. The delegated planner and emitter were unfrozen producer code before this commit, as the plain-assignment route they share was at the b9c pin; this commit pins indexed_field_assignment.rs BYTE-IDENTICAL at 4ff1c20f3a8cb0b0b3a109397d81b2b2b910d4f3, following the ordered_slice_match.rs precedent, so a later edit to what this route lowers needs its own row. ORACLE-FREEZE-MOVES-20261110 INDEXED-FIELD COMPOUND ROUTE (2026-11-10, eb5684db55; DQ THIR-INDEXED-FIELD-COMPOUND-1; a second reader, not its author, re-read the increment against the exact old blob fe0cf10c8d, and a fresh refuter checked this row): a bounded direct-THIR lowering capability expansion. It is NOT BYTE-IDENTICAL and NOT a REFUSES-MORE claim; it is the same class as the ordered shared-slice and Unit-literal accounts below, and it ADMITS NEW lowered bodies. The increment fe0cf10c8d -> f73a1fad76 is +6/-0: one `// Trust:` comment and one early route in LowerCx::lower_assign_op. The route sits after lower_temporary_projection_assign and before the raw-entry field route. It calls indexed_field_assignment.rs::lower_indexed_local_field_assign_op and returns None when that call owns the place. Before, `a[i].f op= rhs` on an SSA local array of a registered flat struct of integer, bool, char, f32 or f64 fields fell through to the `AssignOp(non-local place)` refusal. Now it lowers, in this order: RHS once, then the index once; a re-read of the live array, refused if the array acquired storage or changed type; the bounds assert with its obligation row (a literal out-of-range index then seals Unreachable); ExtractElement and ExtractField; the shared checked emit_arith_binop, with the same overflow, divide-by-zero, MIN/-1 and shift asserts as `x = x op e` (a refusal or divergence owns the route); InsertField, InsertElement and an SSA rebind. After a plan hit, every refusal or divergence (RHS, index, storage change, literal bounds or arithmetic) returns true, so no fallback route re-evaluates an operand. A plan miss returns false and the old routes run unchanged. The plan needs an Index whose base is a VarRef local (index_place_local), so it cannot take a deref place from the raw-entry or `*r` routes. The delegated planner and emitter were unfrozen producer code before this commit, as the plain-assignment route they share was at the b9c pin; this commit pins indexed_field_assignment.rs BYTE-IDENTICAL at 4ff1c20f3a8cb0b0b3a109397d81b2b2b910d4f3, following the ordered_slice_match.rs precedent, so a later edit to what this route lowers needs its own row. To the oracle this SAMPLES MORE: the new bodies reach the unchanged crate-seam differential. No encoder, differential, splice tripwire, admission, proven-output gate or proof-authority token in this file moves, and the direct lane stays ObligationBearingPending with no proof authority. On the opt-in -Ztrust-cg-frontend=trust-ir lane, such bodies may now reach emitted code under the unchanged admission and proven-output gates; that is the new admission this row discloses. A plan miss returns false and the old routes run unchanged.
